name: Glomerular Diseases: Nephritic and Nephrotic Patterns

reference.source: Robbins Basic Pathology 9th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Synpharyngitic visible haematuria within days means IgA nephropathy
Low C3 recovering in 8 weeks fits post streptococcal disease
Childhood abrupt nephrotic syndrome is minimal change until proven otherwise
Crescents demand urgent biopsy and type classification
reference.pathophysiology: Immune complexes, anti basement membrane antibodies or ANCA activated neutrophils injure glomerular capillaries, while podocyte injury alone increases permeability without inflammation in nephrotic diseases. Deposit location (subepithelial, subendothelial, mesangial) maps to syndrome and cause, which is why electron microscopy remains decisive.
additionalDifferentials: IgA nephropathy versus post streptococcal timing and complement
Minimal change versus membranous versus segmental sclerosis
additionalInvestigations: Urinalysis with microscopy for dysmorphic cells and casts
Complement C3 C4 with ANA, ANCA and anti GBM serology
Renal biopsy with light, immunofluorescence and electron microscopy
